hot.title: GLM-5.2: Built for Long-Horizon Tasks
You Don't Need Strong Assumptions: Visual Representation Learning via Temporal Differences
hot.summary: Researchers from UIUC and NYU propose Temporal Difference in Vision (TDV), a self-supervised method for learning visual representations from video by predicting future frame embeddings from past frames and learned motion. This approach, which avoids strong inductive biases, demonstrates improved performance on dense spatial tasks like optical flow and stereo depth compared to existing techniques like DINO and iBOT.

hot.title: Qwen-RobotWorld Technical Report: Unifying Embodied World Modeling through Language-Conditioned Video Generation
hot.summary: The Qwen Team introduces Qwen-RobotWorld, a language-conditioned video world model that unifies diverse embodied intelligence tasks through natural language instructions. The system generates physically grounded future visual trajectories across robotic manipulation, autonomous driving, and indoor navigation, achieving leading performance on multiple established benchmarks while facilitating human-to-robot task transfer.

hot.title: VibeThinker-3B: Exploring the Frontier of Verifiable Reasoning in Small Language Models
hot.summary: VibeThinker-3B, a 3-billion-parameter model from Sina Weibo Inc., achieves advanced verifiable reasoning capabilities, matching or exceeding the performance of significantly larger language models on demanding benchmarks in mathematics, coding, and scientific reasoning. The model scored 94.3 on AIME26 and 80.2 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6, further improving to 97.1 on AIME26 and 99.2 on BruMO25 with Claim-Level Reliability Assessment.

hot.title: DreamX-World 1.0: A General-Purpose Interactive World Model
hot.summary: The DreamX Team developed DreamX-World 1.0, a general-purpose interactive world model that transitions video generation from passive synthesis to dynamic, user-controlled simulation. This model achieved the highest overall scores in basic (84.76) and long-horizon (70.41) evaluations against larger competitors, and was preferred by humans in 57.5-61.9% of cases, while also demonstrating enhanced scene persistence and real-time streaming at up to 16 FPS.

hot.title: Unsafe AI or Consolidated Power: AI’s False Dichotomy
Geometric Action Model for Robot Policy Learning
hot.summary: The Geometric Action Model (GAM) repurposes a pretrained Geometric Foundation Model (GFM) as a unified backbone for language-conditioned robot manipulation, integrating 3D perception, future geometry prediction, and action decoding. This approach improves policy robustness to environmental changes and achieves significantly faster inference speeds, up to 55 times quicker than diffusion-based baselines.

hot.title: HarnessX: A Composable, Adaptive, and Evolvable Agent Harness Foundry
hot.summary: HarnessX is a framework for building composable, adaptive, and evolvable AI agent harnesses that achieved an average absolute gain of +14.5% in agent performance across various configurations. It enables agents to systematically learn and improve their runtime interfaces from execution feedback, including co-evolving with the underlying language model to internalize new strategies.

hot.title: ExpRL: Exploratory RL for LLM Mid-Training
hot.summary: ExpRL, developed by researchers from Stanford University, Carnegie Mellon University, and OpenAI, introduces an on-policy reinforcement learning approach for mid-training large language models by using human-written reference solutions as dense reward scaffolds. This method improves the initial policy for subsequent sparse-reward RL, leading to enhanced reasoning capabilities and achieving 63.41% pass@1 on AIME-2026 after downstream training, outperforming supervised fine-tuning and sparse reward baselines.

hot.title: LaWAM: Latent World Action Models for Efficient Dynamics-Aware Robot Policies
hot.summary: LaWAM (Latent World Action Models) proposes an approach for dynamics-aware robot policies that efficiently predict compact latent visual subgoals, rather than high-dimensional pixel-level future observations. This method enables robots to anticipate action consequences with significantly reduced inference latency and model complexity compared to traditional pixel-space world models, achieving high success rates across diverse manipulation tasks.

hot.title: From AGI to ASI
hot.summary: Researchers at Google DeepMind establish an analytical framework to map the potential evolution of artificial intelligence from AGI to ASI, outlining four technological pathways and six specific bottlenecks. The work provides a research agenda for predicting and managing the development of advanced AI capabilities.

hot.title: Ling and Ring 2.6 Technical Report: Efficient and Instant Agentic Intelligence at Trillion-Parameter Scale
hot.summary: Ling Team and Inclusion AI developed the Ling-2.6 and Ring-2.6 model family, optimized for efficient and scalable agentic intelligence at a trillion-parameter scale. These models deliver low-latency responses and robust reasoning, with Ling-2.6 achieving approximately 4x higher token efficiency and up to 4x faster serving, and Ring-2.6 demonstrating leading performance on agentic coding and search benchmarks.

hot.title: T-Rex: Tactile-Reactive Dexterous Manipulation
hot.summary: Researchers from UC Berkeley, NVIDIA, Stanford, and other institutions developed the T-Rex framework, enabling Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to incorporate high-frequency tactile feedback for dexterous manipulation. This approach achieved an average success rate of 65% across 12 contact-rich tasks, outperforming the strongest baseline by more than 30%.

hot.title: ROVE: Unlocking Human Interventions for Humanoid Manipulation via Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: ROVE, a reinforcement learning framework, empowers humanoid robots to learn complex manipulation skills by effectively utilizing imperfect human interventions. It consistently improved task success rates from 45.0% to 80.0% and 56.7% to 86.7% over three iterative cycles on contact-rich and fine-grained tasks.

hot.title: MiniMax Sparse Attention
hot.summary: MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) offers an efficient, blockwise sparse attention mechanism for large language models, significantly reducing computational cost for ultra-long contexts. It maintains model performance across diverse tasks while achieving notable speedups, such as a 14.2x prefill and 7.6x decoding speedup at 1M context on H800 GPUs, driven by a 28.4x reduction in attention FLOPs.

hot.title: A First-Principles Derivation of LLM Policy Optimization: From Expected Reward to GRPO and Its Structural Extensions
hot.summary: A paper from Nanjing University and Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory introduces a unified, first-principles framework for analyzing large language model (LLM) policy optimization algorithms. It decomposes the expected reward objective into trajectory and reward components, systematically mapping existing methods to reveal their specific interventions and guiding future research by clarifying underlying rationales and interdependencies.

hot.title: UniDDT: Unifying Multimodal Understanding and Generation with Decoupled Diffusion Transformer
hot.summary: UniDDT unifies visual understanding and generation capabilities within a single framework using a decoupled Diffusion Transformer architecture and a unified latent visual space. This model, developed by researchers from Nanjing University and ByteDance Seed, achieves competitive performance across both visual generation benchmarks, reaching up to 0.89 GenEval and 87.1 DPG-Bench, and multimodal understanding benchmarks, scoring 1699.5 on MME and 76.5 on SEEDbench.

hot.title: GameCraft-Bench: Can Agents Build Playable Games End-to-End in a Real Game Engine?
hot.summary: GameCraft-Bench introduces a rigorous benchmark and evaluation framework for assessing coding agents' ability to generate complete, playable games end-to-end within a real game engine, revealing that top agents currently achieve only around 40% of desired functionality. The benchmark leverages Godot 4 and a multimodal judge to evaluate engine-grounded, fully constructed game artifacts based on replayed gameplay interactions.

hot.title: VisualClaw: A Real-Time, Personalized Agent for the Physical World
hot.summary: VisualClaw is a multimodal agent framework that utilizes an edge-side cascaded encoding gate for efficient video processing and a self-evolving skill and memory bank for continual adaptation. It introduces VisualClawArena, a new benchmark for evaluating agents in tool-using, workspace-centric scenarios, demonstrating improved accuracy while significantly reducing VLM API costs by an average of 98.1% compared to full-frame video input.

likes.summary: An AI framework named Arbor enables autonomous research by organizing hypotheses, experimental evidence, and insights into a persistent tree structure. This approach allows agents to manage long-horizon scientific tasks and iteratively improve research artifacts more effectively than existing methods.

likes.title: Breaking Entropy Bounds: Accelerating RL Training via MTP with Rejection Sampling
likes.summary: Bebop, developed by Alibaba's Qwen Team, accelerates large language model reinforcement learning training by enhancing Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) efficiency. It addresses MTP acceptance rate degradation by identifying target model entropy as the dominant factor and introduces an end-to-end Total Variation loss and a pre-RL adaptation strategy, achieving up to 1.8x end-to-end training acceleration.

likes.title: EurekAgent: Agent Environment Engineering is All You Need For Autonomous Scientific Discovery
likes.summary: EUREKAGENT introduces an agent environment engineering paradigm that coordinates off-the-shelf LLM-based CLI agents for autonomous scientific discovery, emphasizing external environmental design over prescriptive workflows. The system achieved new state-of-the-art results across mathematics, kernel engineering, and machine learning tasks through structured permissions, artifacts, budgets, and human-in-the-loop interfaces.

likes.title: EvoArena: Tracking Memory Evolution for Robust LLM Agents in Dynamic Environments
likes.summary: This research introduces EvoArena, a benchmark suite designed to evaluate Large Language Model (LLM) agents in continually evolving environments, alongside EvoMem, a patch-based memory paradigm that explicitly tracks memory evolution. EvoMem consistently enhances agent robustness in dynamic settings, yielding improvements of up to 6.1% in chain-level accuracy on the new benchmark and significantly reducing regressions in software engineering tasks.

likes.title: World Tracing: Generative Pixel-Aligned Geometry Beyond the Visible
likes.summary: World Tracing, developed by World Labs and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, presents a generative pixel-aligned multilayer 3D geometry representation. It reconstructs visible surfaces and completes occluded 3D geometry from 2D inputs, showing improved accuracy on visible surfaces and comprehensive geometry generation for objects, scenes, and dynamic content while supporting various downstream 3D applications.

likes.title: Dense Supervision, Sparse Updates: On the Sparsity and Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
likes.summary: Researchers from Nanjing University and Alibaba Group investigated the parameter updates of On-Policy Distillation (OPD), revealing that it induces small, sparse, and spectrally concentrated modifications to model weights, primarily affecting off-principal directions. These findings indicate that OPD's on-policy data distribution drives a localized "editing" style of parameter refinement, distinct from dense supervised approaches.

likes.title: Can I Buy Your KV Cache?
likes.summary: Researchers from Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen, introduced a "prefill CDN" model, demonstrating that reusing precomputed Key-Value caches for shared document prefixes in Large Language Models is token-exact. This approach achieved 9-50x compute cost savings for repeated document access, offering substantial efficiency gains for long-context applications.

likes.title: RepWAM: World Action Modeling with Representation Visual-Action Tokenizers
likes.summary: RepWAM introduces a representation-centric World Action Model that employs a novel visual-action tokenizer (RepViTok) to create semantically rich latent spaces for robot control. It demonstrated improved success rates in real-world manipulation, achieving up to 80% on 'Push the drawer', and outperformed baselines in simulation benchmarks.

likes.title: MaxProof: Scaling Mathematical Proof with Generative-Verifier RL and Population-Level Test-Time Scaling
likes.summary: MiniMax developed MaxProof, a framework that significantly improves large language models' capabilities in generating competition-level mathematical proofs. This is achieved by integrating a multi-stage trained M3 model, which can generate, verify, and refine proofs, with a population-level test-time scaling method that iteratively evolves and selects solutions. MaxProof enabled the M3 model to surpass human gold-medal thresholds on IMO 2025 and USAMO 2026, boosting its one-shot scores by 8 and 10 points, respectively.

likes.title: Anatomy of Post-Training: Using Interpretability to Characterize Data and Shape the Learning Signal
likes.summary: Researchers introduced a data-centric post-training pipeline for large language models that uses neural network interpretability to audit preference datasets and sculpt the learning signal. This approach effectively diagnosed problematic data patterns in datasets like Dolci, mitigated undesirable stylistic attributes such as over-stylization, and enhanced model safeguards against harmful queries.

likes.title: Agents-K1: Towards Agent-native Knowledge Orchestration
likes.summary: Agents-K1 introduces a unified pipeline to construct agent-native scientific knowledge graphs from raw documents at scale, creating Scholar-KG from 2.46 million papers. The system enhanced multi-hop scientific reasoning for LLMs, with GPT-5.2's rationale accuracy increasing from 41.8% to 66.3% on geoscience research questions, and employs a 4B-parameter extraction model performing comparably to larger LLMs.

likes.title: Rubric-Guided Self-Distillation: Post-Training Without Rubric Verifiers
likes.summary: Introducing Rubric-Guided Self-Distillation (RGSD), a method for post-training large language models on open-ended tasks guided by rubrics, eliminates the need for external LLM verifiers. RGSD achieves rubric satisfaction comparable to judge-based reinforcement learning, while notably reducing computational overhead and leading to more concise responses with fewer unsupported claims.

likes.title: Hy-Embodied-0.5-VLA: From Vision-Language-Action Models to a Real-World Robot Learning Stack
likes.summary: HyVLA-0.5, a comprehensive robot learning stack from Tencent Robotics X and Tencent Hy Team, unifies high-fidelity data collection, VLM-based training, preference-driven policy refinement, and real-world deployment for generalist robots. The system achieved 90.9% success on clean simulated tasks and demonstrated effective cross-embodiment transfer and robust policy improvement via reward-free post-training on real robots.
